name: Nigerian Yoruba commercial video-film production
description: A Nigerian video-film pathway linked local performers and cassette traders to production for home-video circulation.

impact.note: A cassette-based production route for one region's audiences; a cheaper way to make and sell drama, from which the Nigerian video-film industry grew.

date.label: 1988–1991 (accounts differ)
date.basis: Later accounts give three reported years for making the film. Adams gives 1988, Haynes gives 1989, and Ayorinde dates the shoot to 1991.

events.statement: Electronics and cassette dealer Kenneth Nnebue and Yoruba travelling-theatre practitioner Ishola Ogunsola collaborated on Aje Ni Iya Mi. Haynes reports a VHS camera for filming and two videocassette recorders for editing.
events.scope: One production episode in the development of Nigerian Yoruba video film.

evidence.supports: Haynes reports a VHS camera and two VCRs for editing, with an April 1997 personal communication cited.
Haynes identifies Nnebue as a dealer in electronics and blank cassettes who financed and sold Yoruba films on cassette.
Haynes and Okome identify Nnebue and Sola Ogunsola and describe a VHS camera and several VCRs. The equipment account belongs to the same source lineage as Haynes's later accounts.
Misodi cites Haynes (2016, p. 8) for a 1989 collaboration between Nnebue and Yoruba travelling-theatre troupe leader Ishola Ogunsola, and for the filming and editing equipment.
Adams places production in 1988 and describes a stage play by Ogunsola as the source.

earliest_record.rationale: The production episode is the earliest evidenced episode in this record. Its year is disputed.

caveats: This production is one episode in a wider Nigerian video-film practice with earlier experiments. The sources disagree on the shooting year, and the date of the catalogued cassette is approximate. The equipment model, duplication site, domestic retail route and sales volume remain unknown.

research.note: Haynes's article traces the production account to a personal communication in Kaduna in April 1997. His later book is Misodi's source. A separate film-industry interview, family testimony and cassette catalogue inform the distribution evidence.
